notes.1: The printed poem heading is IIII., using four strokes. It is encoded separately from the opening verse. The source spelling inposito is retained.
notes.2: The source prints the contraction ingeniost as one word; it is not silently expanded in the transcription.
notes.3: Both occurrences of castast are printed contractions and retained as written.
notes.6: The source ends this verse with a comma. The punctuation has not been regularized to match the following semicolon.
notes.11: The printed spelling inritare is retained, as is inminet at18.
notes.32: The source places quotation marks around timeo only. Their placement is retained with schematic curly quotes.
notes.35: Ego and feci are separately quoted in the print, with dicere between them. The question continues through the following verse.
notes.37: The printed signature 4* follows this verse at the foot of page51. It is encoded as forme work; the couplet continues on page52.
notes.38: The source capitalizes Urbis here and Martigenae in the next verse.
notes.40: The source prints Iliades Iliadesque; the repeated name is retained without editorial correction.
notes.45: The parenthetical multos dabit is printed inside the verse and retained along with its surrounding commas and final colon.
